mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a stimulative environment for the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction term of HOUST and FEDFUNDS is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market growth, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, which boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.
